More than 100 people gathered at the Indiana Governor's residence in Indianapolis Saturday
afternoon for the No Kings Vote early rally.
As WFYI's Barb Anguiano reports, the event was one of thousands nationwide to promote
nonpartisan voter participation.
With the midterms less than three weeks away, people stood along busy roads,
sharing stories about the importance of voting this election cycle.
For some, the rally was an opportunity to air out their frustrations
against the Trump administration.
Crystal Douglas traveled from Kokomo, Indiana with a group called The Handmaids of Indiana.
She says she felt the urgency to do something.
I feel like people need to be voting for their life.
Like, your life depends on it, because it does.
It was unclear if Governor Mike Braun was inside the residence.
He's not up for reelection until 2028, but is a strong supporter
of President Donald Trump's policies, including immigration enforcement and energy.
For NPR News, I'm Barb Anguiano in Indianapolis.
The White House has signed an order that temporarily halts new sanctions against Russia.
That move comes just days before the sanctions were to take effect,
as NPR's Franco Ordonez reports.
The sanctions were part of a package of financial measures designed to put pressure on Russia
and named after the late Senator Lindsey Graham, who led the effort.
Trump, who signed the legislation last month, put a hold on the implementation,
arguing that the pause was in the national interest.
It follows another controversial announcement Trump made,
that the U.S. would be purchasing diesel fuel from Russia.
Ukrainian President Vladimir Zelensky criticized the decision,
charging that the U.S. is easing pressure on Russia,
just as Russia carries out massive attacks on Ukraine's energy sector.
Zelensky wrote on social media that the Graham-led sanctions would have helped enormously,
and that more pressure is needed on Russia instead of financial rewards.
Franco Ordonez, NPR News.
Residents of Bend, Oregon are trying this weekend to come to terms with a school shooting Thursday
that left three students and one teacher dead.
Oregon Governor Tina Kotak says people from around the country have been offering to help.
I really appreciate all the outpouring nationally of just well wishes
and condolences coming from across the country and people just wanting to know how they can help.
And we're still in that first 48 hours of just trying to understand it.
And it's going to be a couple more days before we know all the details.
Parents, teachers, and many others gathered outside the school on Saturday.
That's where they left flowers, they prayed, and they cried.
Police still have no motive for the shooting by a 16-year-old special needs student.
The shooter was killed by a parent who saw him entering the building.
You're listening to NPR News.
Officials say a number of people were killed and injured
when a major fire broke out at a military base in Alberta, Canada this weekend.
They're not saying how many were hurt or killed,
and so far they don't have a cause, but they say the investigation is very delicate.
The base is a major military training center.
The Trump administration canceled tens of millions in grants
for teen pregnancy prevention earlier this year,
saying they normalized sexual activity for minors.
But a new legal complaint alleges the administration then sent almost all of that money
to a single contractor through a secretive, rushed process.
MPR's Selena Simmons-Duffin reports.
The complaint was filed by Hennepin County, Minnesota,
one of the teen pregnancy prevention grantees
whose federal funding was canceled earlier this year.
It alleges that the Department of Health and Human Services
awarded $86 million to Guidehouse, a private equity-backed consulting firm,
and did so without the usual competitive process
local health departments and organizations have used for years.
Democracy Forward is representing the county.
Sky Perriman is the CEO.
Our focus is going to continue to be to use every legal tool we can
to ensure the program's administered as Congress intended.
The bid protest aims to block the award to Guidehouse.
The first hearing is scheduled for Tuesday in the U.S. Court of Federal Claims.
Selena Simmons-Duffin, NPR News, Washington.
Gabby Williams converted to free throws
with less than two minutes left to put Golden State ahead
as the Valkyries held off the Atlanta Dream 68-64 Saturday.
Williams also finished the game with 26 points.
Game two in the best of seven WNBA Finals
takes place Monday night in San Francisco.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.
